title: An Encoding Scheme to Enlarge Practical DNA Storage Capacity by Reducing Primer-Payload Collisions
problem: DNA storage systems experience primer-payload collisions that reduce practical storage capacity. Increasing encoding density alone is insufficient without addressing collision-induced inefficiencies in sequence utilization.
motivation: DNA offers ultra-high storage density and exceptional durability for long-term archival, making capacity optimization critical for practical deployment.
method: The paper proposes a novel encoding scheme that systematically reduces primer-payload collisions during DNA synthesis and sequencing. The approach improves DNA sequence utilization efficiency by preventing primers and payloads from interfering with each other, addressing multiple facets of storage capacity beyond density metrics alone.
key_novelty: An encoding scheme specifically designed to mitigate primer-payload collisions as the primary mechanism for increasing practical DNA storage capacity.
contributions: Encoding scheme to reduce primer-payload collisions in DNA storage
Method to improve practical storage capacity beyond density increases
Analysis of collision-related bottlenecks in DNA storage systems

metrics.other: storage capacity improvement (detailed metrics not provided in abstract)

primary_theme: DNA storage encoding via collision reduction
